description: NLA-mosaic: mathematical algorithms with nonlinear invariants

programs.name: pell
programs.purpose: Generate successive positive Pell-equation solutions by multiplication by 3+2*sqrt(2).
programs.source: Keith Conrad, Pell's Equation I, section 4, New Solutions from Old Solutions. https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/ugradnumthy/pelleqn1.pdf
programs.notes: Initialize (x,y)=(1,0). All updates use the old state.

programs.name: fibonacci
programs.purpose: Generate consecutive Fibonacci numbers, exposing Cassini's alternating determinant.
programs.source: Polar documentation, Fibonacci loop and quartic invariant. https://github.com/probing-lab/polar#introduction
programs.notes: Initialize (a,b)=(0,1). The quadratic a^2+a*b-b^2 alternates signs; its square is constant.

programs.name: fibonacci_sign
programs.purpose: Generate consecutive Fibonacci numbers and explicitly track Cassini's sign.
programs.source: Polar documentation, Fibonacci loop and quartic invariant; this sign-variable variant is our adaptation. https://github.com/probing-lab/polar#introduction
programs.notes: Initialize (a,b,sign)=(0,1,-1); negate sign each iteration. Also sign^2=1.

programs.name: markov
programs.purpose: Walk the Markov-triple tree by alternating two mutation/permutation branches.
programs.source: (Un)Solvable Loop Analysis, Formal Methods in System Design (2024), Example 39, markov-triples-toggle. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10703-024-00455-0
programs.notes: Our adaptation accepts four valid initial triples and either starting branch. A coordinate guard stops growth before C updates overflow.

programs.name: fibonacci_trace
programs.notes: Our adaptation accepts bounded initial coordinates and stores their initial conserved polynomial as constant.

programs.name: berggren
programs.purpose: Generate Pythagorean triples by following the three Berggren matrix branches.
programs.notes: Start at (3,4,5). Our input path encodes branch choices as base-3 digits; each branch uses old-state temporaries.

programs.name: continued_fraction
programs.purpose: Compute continued-fraction convergents with changing partial quotients.
programs.source: F. Al-Faisal, Elementary Number Theory, Proposition 30.7. https://math.uwaterloo.ca/~f2alfais/notes/pm340-notes.pdf
programs.notes: Start (p,r,q,s)=(1,0,0,1). Our path digits select partial quotients 1,2,3. p*s-r*q alternates +1/-1.

programs.name: continued_fraction_sign
programs.purpose: Compute continued-fraction convergents and explicitly track their determinant sign.
programs.source: F. Al-Faisal, Elementary Number Theory, Proposition 30.7. https://math.uwaterloo.ca/~f2alfais/notes/pm340-notes.pdf
programs.notes: Start (p,r,q,s,sign)=(1,0,0,1,1). Our path digits select partial quotients 1,2,3. Also sign^2=1.

programs.name: chebyshev
programs.purpose: Evaluate consecutive first-kind Chebyshev polynomials by their three-term recurrence.
programs.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, sections 18.5 and 18.9. https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.5 ; https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.9
programs.notes: Start (a,b)=(1,t). t is an immutable input, so the conserved relation has degree 3. The displayed identity is derived from the recurrence.

programs.name: chebyshev_pair
programs.purpose: Evaluate first-kind T_n(t) together with second-kind U_(n-1)(t).
programs.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, section 18.5. https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.5
programs.notes: Start (T,U)=(1,0), interpreting U_-1=0. t is an immutable input, so the conserved relation has degree 4. Our paired update and identity are derived from the definitions.

programs.name: nagata
programs.purpose: Iterate the Nagata polynomial automorphism, whose expanded x update has degree 5.
programs.notes: Our adaptation accepts bounded initial coordinates and stores x0*z0+y0^2 as constant. z is unchanged, but z0 is not part of vtrace1.

programs.name: binomial
programs.purpose: Compute a row of binomial coefficients using the multiplicative recurrence.
programs.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, equation 26.3.6. https://dlmf.nist.gov/26.3#E6
programs.notes: Start (k,c,prev)=(0,1,0). c=binomial(N,k); prev holds the preceding coefficient. Division is exact on reachable states and follows multiplication.

programs.name: welford
programs.purpose: Compute an online mean and corrected sum of squared deviations (M2).
programs.source: B. P. Welford, Note on a Method for Calculating Corrected Sums of Squares and Products, Technometrics 4(3), 419-420 (1962). https://doi.org/10.1080/00401706.1962.10490022
programs.notes: Our deterministic sample stream uses base, step, and n. Auxiliary sum and sumsq expose prefix statistics. The identities hold over exact reals; ordinary C doubles can produce nonzero rounding residuals. M2 is an unnormalized sum; sample variance is M2/(n-1) for n>1.

programs.name: symplectic_euler
programs.arithmetic: exact dyadic C doubles within input bounds
programs.purpose: Advance a harmonic oscillator using momentum-first symplectic Euler steps.
programs.source: E. Hairer and G. Vilmart, Computing the Long Term Evolution of the Solar System with Geometric Numerical Integrators, section 3. https://www.unige.ch/~vilmart/snapshots-2017-009.pdf
programs.notes: Our momentum-first ordering uses the negative cross term; its sign/coefficient were derived and checked independently. energy stores the initial modified energy. Steps are 1/4,1/2,3/4; bounded dyadic runs preserve the observed values exactly.
